wiki.extract: The Giza pyramid complex in Egypt is home to the Great Pyramid, the pyramid of Khafre, and the pyramid of Menkaure, along with their associated pyramid complexes and the Great Sphinx. All were built during the Fourth Dynasty of the Old Kingdom of ancient Egypt, between c. 2600 – c. 2500 BC. The site also includes several temples, cemeteries, and the remains of a workers' village.
A sphinx is a mythical creature with the head of a human, the body of a lion, and the wings of an eagle.

The Karnak Temple Complex, commonly known as Karnak, comprises a vast mix of temples, pylons, chapels, and other buildings near Luxor, Egypt. Construction at the complex began during the reign of Senusret I in the Middle Kingdom and continued into the Ptolemaic Kingdom, although most of the extant buildings date from the New Kingdom. The area around Karnak was the ancient Egyptian Ipet-isut and the main place of worship of the 18th Dynastic Theban Triad, with the god Amun as its head.

The Valley of the Kings, also known as the Valley of the Gates of the Kings, is an area in Egypt where, for a period of nearly 500 years from the Eighteenth Dynasty to the Twentieth Dynasty, rock-cut tombs were excavated for pharaohs and powerful nobles under the New Kingdom of ancient Egypt.

Abu Simbel is a historic site comprising two massive rock-cut temples in the village of Abu Simbel, Aswan Governorate, Upper Egypt, near the border with Sudan. It is located on the western bank of Lake Nasser, about 230 km (140 mi) southwest of Aswan. Its latitude of 22° 20′ 13″ N is 1.0978°, which are 122 km, south of the tropic of Cancer.

The Cairo International Film Festival is an annual internationally accredited film festival held in Cairo, Egypt. Founded in 1976, the festival is the only international competitive feature film festival recognized by the FIAPF in Africa and the Arab world as well as the oldest in this category. The festival regularly draws tens of thousands of visitors each year. Cairo is held annually at the Cairo Opera House and under the auspices of the Egyptian Ministry of Culture.

Sham Ennessim is a festival marking the beginning of spring, celebrated by Egyptians of all religions. It is an official public holiday in Egypt. Sham Ennessim always falls on Easter Monday, which is the day after Easter, in accordance with the Orthodox Church. The Arabic name Sham Ennesim translates into "Smelling in the Zephyrs".

Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. It is observed by Muslims worldwide as a month of fasting (sawm), communal prayer (salah), reflection, study of the Quran, charity, and strengthening community ties. It is also the month in which the Quran is believed to have been revealed to the Islamic prophet Muhammad, known as Laylat al-Qadr. The annual observance of Ramadan is regarded as one of the five pillars of Islam and lasts 29 to 30 days, from one sighting of the crescent moon to the next.
August is the eighth month of the year in the Julian and Gregorian calendars. Its length is 31 days.

food_writeup: Egyptian cuisine features staples like ful medames (fava beans), koshari (a lentil and rice dish), and molokhia (a leafy green soup), reflecting a blend of Mediterranean and Middle Eastern flavors.
brief_history: Egypt is one of the world's oldest civilizations, known for its ancient pharaohs, monumental architecture, and contributions to writing and governance. It was later ruled by Greeks, Romans, Arabs, and Ottomans before gaining independence in the 20th century.
current_conflicts: Egypt faces challenges related to regional security, including concerns over the Nile River water rights and counterterrorism efforts in the Sinai Peninsula.

commentary.inflation_management: Egypt's inflation is a chronicle of delayed devaluations. It ran at 10-16% through the 2011-2016 turmoil as the central bank burned reserves defending the pound. The November 2016 float, under the $12 billion IMF program, sent inflation to 23.5% in 2017 and 20.9% in 2018 before it subsided to 4.5-5.7% in 2020-21. The 2022 Ukraine shock and three step devaluations reignited it: 24.4% in 2023 and a series high of 33.3% in 2024. The March 2024 decision to finally float the pound (with a 600bp rate hike to 27.25%) broke the cycle; inflation is projected at 20.4% for 2025 and falling. The central bank now targets inflation with a flexible exchange rate, but credibility will take years to rebuild after repeated broken peg promises.
commentary.debt_management: Egypt's debt has been chronically high and crisis-prone. It fell to 66.8% of GDP in 2008 on pre-crisis growth, then climbed through revolution, currency defense, and mega-project spending to 97.8% in 2017, the series high. The 2016 IMF program brought it down to 79.8% by 2019, but COVID, the Ukraine war's import bill, and renewed pound defense pushed it back to 95.7% in 2023. The March 2024 package (IMF $8 billion plus a $35 billion UAE Ras El-Hekma investment deal) stabilized the position, with debt projected at 86.7% in 2025. Sustainability hinges on the exchange rate staying flexible: every defense of the pound has ended in a debt spike, and interest costs consume a huge share of revenues.

key_events.event: Revolution ousted Mubarak; tourism and investment collapsed, starting a decade of fiscal strain.
Pound floated under a $12 billion IMF program; inflation surged to 23.5% (2017).
COVID-19; Egypt was one of few economies to keep growing, but debt rose.
Ukraine war triggered capital flight; three devaluations and a $3 billion IMF deal (December 2022).
Sisi re-elected (December 2023); Gaza war and Houthi attacks slashed Suez Canal revenues.
February 2024: $35 billion UAE Ras El-Hekma deal; March 2024: pound floated, rates hiked 600bp, IMF program expanded to $8 billion.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The base case is gradual disinflation and debt decline if the flexible exchange rate holds, the IMF's third program in a decade stays on track, and Gulf financing continues. Upside comes from private-sector growth and energy exports; downside is familiar: if the pound is re-pegged or military-linked enterprises crowd out reform, the next external shock restarts the crisis cycle. Uncertainty is moderate: the 2024 package was decisive, but Egypt has exited IMF programs early before.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
